# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 18 (Bu-Vb Pc18)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc18
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 18
**Title (English, from literature):** Sitting down on an upper story
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vehāsakuṭi Sikkhāpada* is the eighteenth training rule in the *Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*. The rule stipulates that a monk who sits or lies down on a bed or bench with detachable or unfastened legs on an unplanked upper storey of an accommodation belonging to the Saṅgha commits an offense requiring expiation or confession (*pācittiya*) [Dhammika, Broken Buddha]. In contemporary discussions on the classification of monastic discipline, this rule is occasionally highlighted as an example of an explicitly practical or minor precept (*khuddānukhuddaka-sikkhāpada*) designed to prevent physical hazards and structural accidents within the monastic dwelling [Dhammika, Broken Buddha].

Complete parallels to this rule are preserved widely across early Buddhist monastic traditions, appearing not only in the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, the *Parivāra*, and the corresponding *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Pācittiya 114), but also in the Vinayas of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahāsāṃghika, Mahīśāsaka, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Sarvāstivāda, and Kāśyapīya traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan. An English translation of the rule and its full *Vibhaṅga* analysis has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
